entries.claim: Per-well read/UMI/gene QC with plate/positional diagnostics that drops low-quality wells and treats wells as samples, not cells.
Compound- and dose-resolved differential expression versus matched vehicle with FDR control and a mandatory vehicle-versus-vehicle null contrast.

Signed, lowest-dose-referenced concentration-response modeling with a transcriptomic point of departure reported only when a compound has at least four doses, positive dose association, and a benchmark crossing; flat responses are explicitly null.
Gene-set and TF activity scoring by univariate linear model over supplied gene sets.
Perturbational signatures and correlation-based mechanism-of-action clustering with an export for optional connectivity analysis.
Input routing across caller-selected counts and FASTQ modes that rejects incomplete input sets.
Hard stops on barcode/whitelist mismatch and non-identifiable batch-confounded designs, with no fabricated tPOD below four doses.

Runtime-component identity is kept separate from version capture: the DESeq2 package version is queried and persisted when DESeq2 is used, and the R interpreter version or an installed boolean is never reused as the package version.

capabilities.trigger: Use for DRUG-seq or plate-based bulk RNA-seq compound screens (counts+platemap or barcoded FASTQ): per-well QC, compound/dose differential expression, perturbational signatures with MoA clustering, dose-response/tPOD, and pathway/TF activity. Not for single-cell or Perturb-seq data; wells are samples, not cells.

inference_readiness.design_identifiability_check: scripts/design_preflight.py checks that no condition is confounded with a whole plate; scripts/well_qc.py check_identifiability stops the run otherwise
inference_readiness.experimental_unit: well (a treated well-group versus matched vehicle wells on the same plate)
inference_readiness.permutation_support_check: the vehicle-versus-vehicle null contrast is the empirical negative control and must return approximately zero DEGs
inference_readiness.replicate_type: replicate wells per condition (technical/plate-level unit that may not be fully independent biological replicates)

resource_identity.not_applicable_reason: The run emits no external accessions, citations, or versioned resource identifiers whose surrounding metadata must be cross-checked; every output is derived from caller-selected inputs.

caveats.statement: Treating each well as a single cell (running a scRNA/Perturb-seq pipeline on well pseudobulk), or ranking hits by raw p-value with no vehicle-versus-vehicle null, lets plate position and library-size differences read as compound biology; this skill uses well-level bulk DESeq2 against per-plate matched vehicle and a mandatory null contrast under the same plate/edge adjustment terms. The run hard-stops when that null exceeds the pre-specified maximum of 5 apparent DEGs.

A wrong barcode whitelist or a transposed plate map collapses the barcode assignment rate; below threshold the run stops and asks you to reconcile the whitelist and plate map rather than mislabeling wells.
Plate row/column/edge gradients can masquerade as dose effects; the run flags positional confounding when plate position explains an outsized share of well-to-well variance.
Low-count genes yield unstable, inflated fold-changes; hits below the baseMean floor are flagged as low-expression rather than ranked as effects.

Top-dose transcriptional signatures can reflect cytotoxicity, global transcription/translation inhibition, or general stress rather than compound-specific pharmacology; the report must quote the artifact-derived limitation and disclose whether a viability measurement was available.
When a treatment condition is confounded with a whole plate the effect is not identifiable; the run stops rather than reporting a plate effect as compound biology.

The transcriptomic point of departure is method-sensitive by roughly an order of magnitude and requires at least four doses; the method and benchmark response are recorded and no tPOD is invented below four doses.
On targeted panels, off-panel genes are absent rather than zero; the run discloses whether values are measured or imputed so absent genes are not read as unchanged.

Connectivity/MoA against CMap or LINCS is not computed offline here. The exported signatures can be analyzed with signature-reversal-lincs, which reports at least two metrics under its own data-use terms.

The R interpreter version and the DESeq2 package version are different identifiers (for example R 4.4.3 versus DESeq2 1.46.0); when DESeq2 is used the run queries and persists the DESeq2 package version separately and never prints the R interpreter version or an installed boolean as the package version.

inputs: counts.tsv - genes (rows) by wells (columns) matrix of integer UMI counts; the header lists well IDs matching platemap.csv.

platemap.csv - one row per well with columns well_id, compound, dose_uM, timepoint_h, replicate, plate_id, row, col, and semantic is_control. Flag the matched negative-control vehicle independently of its compound name; mixed global vehicle identities stop before modeling.
genesets.gmt - caller-selected MSigDB or curated gene sets for activity scoring.
Optional FASTQ front end - R1 (well barcode + UMI) and R2 (cDNA) FASTQ, a barcode whitelist (barcodes.txt), and a reference.tsv of probe/target genes.
Wells are experimental units (samples), not cells; dose is in micromolar; counts are UMI-deduplicated integers.

workflow.instruction: Run `scripts/well_qc.py` for per-well UMI/gene metrics, data-driven low-quality-well dropping, and plate row/column/edge positional diagnostics; stop with not_computable when the barcode assignment rate is below threshold. Success: `tables/well_qc.csv` with one row per well and the dropped-well list.
workflow.title: Per-well and plate QC

workflow.instruction: Run `scripts/design_preflight.py` to check per-condition replicate wells and design identifiability, stopping when a condition is confounded with a whole plate; normalize with a plate (and optional position) covariate. Success: `tables/design_preflight.csv` and an identifiable design.
workflow.title: Experimental design and normalization

workflow.instruction: Run the bundled `scripts/de_deseq2.R` for each compound-by-dose versus matched vehicle at padj<0.05 and absolute log2 fold-change above 1, applying a baseMean floor so low-count genes are flagged not ranked. Success: `tables/de_all_contrasts.csv` and `tables/de_summary.csv`.
workflow.title: Differential expression contrasts with FDR control

workflow.instruction: Fit the mandatory NULL_VEHICLE_vs_VEHICLE contrast by splitting the is_control-flagged vehicle wells with the same plate/edge adjustment terms as treatment contrasts. Require a full-rank null design and apply the pre-specified `scientific_logic.MAX_NULL_DEGS=5` delivery gate before any downstream analysis. Success: exactly one null row, `null_contrast.status=passed`, and `null_contrast.n_deg<=5`; otherwise hard-stop.
workflow.title: Vehicle-versus-vehicle null contrast

workflow.instruction: Run `scripts/dose_response.py` to orient top-dose DEGs by their signed top-dose direction, subtract the lowest tested dose as a within-compound reference, and interpolate the tPOD at the benchmark response only when at least four doses show positive dose association. A flat or non-associated response is explicitly null. Success: `tables/dose_response.csv` with a pinned method, tPODs, or an explicit null reason.
workflow.title: Concentration-response and transcriptomic POD

workflow.instruction: Run `scripts/signatures_moa.py` to build per-compound signatures, cluster compounds by signature correlation, and export query signatures for optional analysis in signature-reversal-lincs. Success: `tables/moa_clusters.csv` and `tables/query_signatures.json`.
workflow.title: Perturbational signatures, MOA clustering, and connectivity export

workflow.instruction: Run the bundled `scripts/activity_ulm.R` to score gene-set and TF activity per compound by univariate linear model over the supplied gene sets. Rank the headline set only by the version-controlled maximum absolute ULM t-value in `scientific_logic.PATHWAY_RANKING_METRIC`, preserving its signed t-value for interpretation; no runtime or review-time branch may change that metric. Success: `tables/activity_scores.csv` with activity t-values.
workflow.title: Pathway and TF-activity scoring

source_assertions_not_applicable_reason: The packaged run ingests only caller-selected counts/platemap or FASTQ inputs; it makes no computation-critical claim about an external database record, genome build, coordinate convention, or literature value. Public reference datasets (LINCS/CMap, MSigDB) are referenced only for optional caller-selected inputs or later connectivity analysis and are not silently ingested or asserted by this run.

starting_task.decision_context: Early drug-discovery triage: prioritize compounds, doses, and mechanisms for follow-up and decide which apparent hits are real versus plate/position or library-size artifacts, at hypothesis-generating strength.
starting_task.deliverables: A branded PDF report_drug-seq-analysis.pdf at the results root with one qualitative workflow infographic, plus infographic.png, infographic_prompt_binding.json, machine-readable tables tables/well_qc.csv, tables/de_all_contrasts.csv, tables/activity_scores.csv, tables/dose_response.csv, tables/moa_clusters.csv, and the facts artifact report_facts.json.
starting_task.objective: Quantify per-compound, per-dose transcriptional responses versus matched vehicle with FDR control, derive perturbational signatures and MoA clustering, and estimate dose-response and the transcriptomic point of departure, treating wells as experimental samples rather than cells.
starting_task.subject_input: A DRUG-seq / plate-based bulk RNA-seq compound screen: a genes-by-wells matrix of integer UMI counts (counts.tsv) and a platemap.csv giving each well's compound, dose_uM, timepoint_h, replicate, plate_id, row, col, and is_control vehicle flag; optionally barcoded FASTQ with a whitelist and reference for the demultiplexing front end.
starting_task.user_prompt: Assess per-well quality in a DRUG-seq compound screen, quantify compound- and dose-resolved differential expression, and summarize perturbational signatures, dose response, and pathway activity.
